subject: 7BD7CC169D32E75C6079CAD5883AFA43
introduction: The Báb and Bahá’u’lláh were born into Shí‘ih Islam, and their writings and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s talks are full of its practices: the five prayers and the call to prayer, Ramadan, the pilgrimage and the Black Stone, the rosary, the mosques of Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem. This guide gathers such references. Some are devotional, some explain a rite as a symbol, some record how the new revelation changed a law (congregational prayer is ended), and some are sharp criticism of observance that has become habit, or of the party that persecuted the Báb. The criticism is the prophets’ and the Qur’an’s own: “their heart is far from me”, “woe unto worshippers who are heedless of their prayer”, “it is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West”. A reader should keep reading 42 in its setting: it speaks of those who killed the Báb, not of Muslims or Shí‘ihs as such.
questions: The readings both honour Islamic practices and criticize how they were kept. What exactly is criticized?
The Qur’an itself warns worshippers “heedless of their prayer”. Why does every tradition need that warning?
What is the argument of reading 34 for praying alone? What would a Muslim, or the Psalmist, say for the congregation?
Reading 23 calls a rite a symbol. Does understanding a rite as symbolic strengthen or weaken its observance?
How should a reader today take the harsh language of readings 41 to 43?

outside.why: Nothing to show but outward observances. This people honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.
Bring no more vain oblations; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with.
Playing with the rosary has become a habit. When ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

Prayer, alms and pilgrimage are signs of His revelation. It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West; but righteous is he who believeth, and giveth wealth, and observeth proper worship.
All is performed to attain His good pleasure. The reward of deeds depends upon the intentions.
“By the reality of bowing and prostration.” O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker.
Praise to God who sent down the Furqán. The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur’an, a guidance for mankind.
The heat produced by the fast. Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off evil.
The breaking of the fast, a time of joy. When thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face; that thou appear not unto men to fast.
The obligatory prayers by their hours. Seven times a day do I praise thee.
Establish worship at the two ends of the day and in some watches of the night.
God’s remembrance in the call to prayer. Worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity, but verily remembrance of Allah is more important.
A dream of raising the call to prayer in a great mosque. Herbert’s list of what prayer is: God’s breath in man returning to his birth, the soul in paraphrase, heart in pilgrimage.
Numbers none can reckon gather at Thy House. Pilgrimage to the House is a duty unto Allah for mankind, for him who can find a way thither.
The Black Stone: simple obedience to the Prophet. The first Sanctuary appointed for mankind was that at Becca, a blessed place.
Circumambulation is a symbol. Of the sacrifices at the pilgrimage: their flesh and their food reach not Allah, but the devotion from you reacheth Him.
The Aqṣá Mosque speaks. Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship.
Obligatory prayer is to be said individually; congregational prayer is annulled. When thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret.

The Psalmist’s instinct, and Islam’s Friday, is the other: in the congregations will I bless the Lord. What is lost when prayer is no longer said in rows behind a leader, and what do the readings think is gained?
Reverence forgotten in holy places. Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools.
Ramadan was once so strictly kept that eating was punished. The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath. Is strictness of that kind a sign of a law’s health?
Dervish ceremonies observed with a sceptical eye. Rúmí, whose order they are: I regard not the outside and the words, I regard the inside and the state of heart.
Names have become idols. Whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones.
They still go to the mosque and imagine they remember God. Woe unto worshippers who are heedless of their prayer; who would be seen at worship.
Hosea had said it of the Temple’s worshippers long before: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

shortfall: The remaining readings are descriptions of rites, months and places, or severe judgments on a party; the first need no companion, and for the second none was sought beyond the prophets’ own.
